item.subject: science
item.chapter_label: Earth, Sun and the apparent motion of the sky
item.stem:
Aisha sketches the stars at 7 p.m. in May. In November she looks again at 7 p.m. The night sky at that same clock time has changed. On one May night she also compares the 7 p.m. sky with the sky at 1 a.m. She is deciding whether Earth’s rotation on its axis or Earth’s revolution around the Sun explains the month-to-month change at the same clock time.

Which claim is correct?

options.A: The change from May’s 7 p.m. sky to November’s 7 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s revolution around the Sun.
options.B: The change from May’s 7 p.m. sky to November’s 7 p.m. sky comes mainly from Earth’s rotation on its axis.
options.C: Rotation is Earth moving around the Sun; revolution is Earth turning on its own axis.
options.D: The entire difference between May’s 7 p.m. sky and May’s 1 a.m. sky is caused only by Earth’s revolution around the Sun.
